17. **How cities become free.** The ways a city breaks free of its master ("How cities become free"): conquered land not yet absorbed that revolts and breaks free ("Revolt follows conditions, not dice"); a governor who turns with the levies he raised, or a commander who keeps his army, and rules a city of his own, the new Idrimi; and a revolt with no one at its head raising a ruler from its own people ("A head rises where men lack one"). Each new free city is a power with a seat of its own, by the rules of item 11+. Built after item 13, since it needs governors and commanders, and after 11b's risen heads. Split from the city-states item on 21 October 2026, when city-states as powers moved forward to item 11+; a vassal who stops paying is free in practice already there. With revolt comes the gate opened from within, when a besieged city's hunger breaks its loyalty ("How long a siege lasts"). And an army living off the land angers its people (Haakon, 29 October 2026: "An army eating from the actual citizens stores then should make them pretty unhappy?", and to the design session's takes, "Yes, to all, expertly!"): troops taking food raise unrest by how much they take, their own king's included; every province carries unrest, the homeland too, though absorbed land starts loyal and needs far more to rise; each army buys its food where it stands by leave or takes it, as its king's order says once it arrives, but by need when it has no gold to buy with, and by its commander's choice once it has one, who may keep the gold sent for food and take anyway (Haakon, 29 October 2026: "But remember, when you say a king decides how his army supplies himself. Information time travel stoll applies. He can tell them to buy, but if he hasn't sent them enough money to buy with, they will do what they must to eat. And an army with an assigned commander (a character) the commander has the final say on following orders or not. He may keep any money meant for food, and just take instead."); and a ruler whose land was taken from remembers it as a grievance ("Revolt follows conditions, not dice" under War, "Armies need food as well as pay" under Land, people and economy). The script kings weigh buying against taking, and the item's report shows how often each is chosen and how often a homeland province rose. **Stop for review.**
